h: Choosing Your Room and Exploring the Area
p: With three rooms to pick from, it's worth thinking about your group before you book. If it's your first escape room or you've got younger players, ask which room is the friendliest for beginners. If you're seasoned puzzlers, go for the toughest challenge and see if you can set a decent time. Groups of four or five often hit the sweet spot, enough brains to share the work without people tripping over each other.

A tip that experienced escapers swear by: keep the room tidy as you search. Pile up used clues and items in one place so you don't waste time picking up the same things twice. And appoint someone to keep an eye on the clock, so you know when it's time to ask for a hint rather than burning ten precious minutes on one padlock.

West Wickham sits on the edge of the London Borough of Bromley, where the city starts to give way to green countryside. West Wickham Common and nearby Hayes Common have woodland and heath for a good leg-stretch after an hour of brain work. Keston Common, a little further south, has its lovely ponds and the spot of the Wilberforce Oak, where William Wilberforce is said to have decided to bring the abolition of the slave trade before Parliament.

For a fascinating extra, Down House, Charles Darwin's family home at Downe, is a short drive away and is run by English Heritage. You can see his study and walk the Sandwalk, the path where he did his thinking. High Elms Country Park nearby is great for nature trails. West Wickham station is on the line from London, so it's easy to reach by train too.
